        Idea:
Implement two-tier shot groups on the video editor timeline: suggested (inferred, dashed border) and pinned (persistent, solid border).

## Core concept
The current useShotGroups inference becomes 'suggested' groups shown with dashed borders. Users can promote them to 'pinned' groups which are stored in timeline config, persist across refresh, and enable advanced features.

## Data model
PinnedShotGroup stored in timelineConfig:
- shotId, trackId, clipIds[], mode: 'images' | 'video', videoAssetKey?, imageClipSnapshot? (for swap-back)

## When pinned groups are created (explicit + implicit):

### Explicit:
1. Right-click a suggested group → 'Pin as Shot Group' - writes PinnedShotGroup to config
2. Drop a shot from shot list/gallery onto timeline - creates pinned group with images expanded as clips

### Implicit (auto-pin):
3. 'Switch to Final Video' on a suggested group - auto-pins first (snapshots image clips), then swaps to video mode
4. When an image is added to a shot that already has a pinned group on the timeline - auto-inserts the new image clip into the pinned group's track at the right position

## Visual distinction:
- Suggested: dashed border, lighter color (current border style → dashed)
- Pinned: solid border, full color (current styling), shot name visible

## Pinned group behavior:
- Clips drag together as a unit (grouped drag)
- Image ↔ video toggle: switch stores snapshot of image clips, restores on switch-back. Single applyEdit each direction.
- Shot image sync: when images are added/removed from a shot, pinned group auto-updates (subscribe to shot changes via realtime or ShotsContext)
- Context menu: Pin/Unpin, Switch to Video/Images, Jump to Shot, Generate Video

## Key architectural decisions:
- pinnedShotGroups stored in TimelineData (persisted via timeline config, undoable)
- useShotGroups still runs for inference but pinned groups take priority (suppress inferred for same shot+track)
- PinnedShotGroup clipIds are the source of truth for which clips belong to the group
- When a pinned group exists, the shot group overlay reads from the pinned data, not from inference

- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useShotGroups.ts - current inference
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useSwitchToFinalVideo.ts - current swap (to be replaced)

User notes and answers:
- Addressing critique flags:

FLAG-001 (suppression granularity): Use clipIds-based suppression instead of shotId:trackId. A pinned group stores its clipIds. When filtering inferred groups, suppress any inferred group whose clipIds are a subset of a pinned group's clipIds. This handles multiple clusters of the same shot on one track.

FLAG-002/correctness-2/callers-1 (applyEdit config mutations): Add a new mutation type to TimelineEditMutation: { type: 'pinnedShotGroups', pinnedShotGroups: PinnedShotGroup[] }. This is cleaner than trying to squeeze metadata into the existing config or rows paths. The commit handler reads current data, replaces pinnedShotGroups, and rebuilds. For switch-to-video which needs BOTH rows changes AND pinnedShotGroups changes, use the existing type:'rows' mutation but add an optional pinnedShotGroupsOverride field.

FLAG-003 (grouped drag): Defer group expansion to after drag threshold is crossed, not on pointer-down. On pointer-down, just record that the clip is in a pinned group. On first pointermove past threshold, expand draggedClipIds to include all group clips.

FLAG-004/scope-1/all_locations-3 (shot drop DnD): Add a new drag type 'shot' to shared DnD utilities. Add drag source in shot list components. Add acceptance in onTimelineDragOver. This is Phase 6 and can be a follow-up if needed.

FLAG-005/all_locations-1 (migrateToFlatTracks): Explicitly update migrateToFlatTracks to preserve pinnedShotGroups. It currently rebuilds config with an allowlist - add pinnedShotGroups to that list.

all_locations-2 (rowsToConfig callers): Update render-bounds.validation.test.ts and any other direct callers.

issue_hints-1 (clip lifecycle): When a clip in a pinned group is manually deleted, remove it from the group's clipIds. If clipIds becomes empty, remove the pinned group. If in video mode and the video clip is deleted, auto-switch back to images from snapshot if available, otherwise remove the group.

issue_hints-2 (hasFinalVideo guard): Preserve the existing guard - Switch to Video only shows when finalVideoMap.get(shotId) exists. Switch to Images only shows when mode is video.

conventions-1 (reuse insertion helpers): Reuse useAssetManagement helpers for shot drop clip creation rather than hand-building.

conventions-2 (mutation model): All pinned group changes go through applyEdit, never direct mutation of dataRef.current. This preserves undo/history.

  "meta_commentary": "Execution guidance:\n\n1. **Start with T1+T2 sequentially** \u2014 they're the foundation. Read types/index.ts, serialize.ts, migrate.ts, timeline-data.ts, and useTimelineCommit.ts before making changes. The customEffects pattern is your template.\n\n2. **T3 is the highest-risk task.** The 'rows' branch with pinnedShotGroupsOverride is where critique flags converge. Key insight: after materializeData() produces new data from rows, you MUST set pinnedShotGroups on the resulting config and THEN rebuild TimelineData from it (or ensure assembleTimelineData sees the final config). Post-hoc mutation of an already-assembled TimelineData leaves stableSignature stale. The cleanest approach: materializeData returns a config, apply override to config, then pass to buildDataFromCurrentRegistry.\n\n3. **T10 (clip lifecycle)** is second highest risk. The plan says \"post-commit reconcile\" but that creates double history. Instead: make reconciliation part of materializeData itself. When it rebuilds rows, check if any pinned group clipIds reference clips no longer in the new rows. Clean them in the same data pass, before commitData. Zero extra undo entries.\n\n4. **T12 (grouped drag)** has THREE code paths to handle: (a) same-track multi-drag via type:'rows' \u2014 add pinnedShotGroupsOverride with updated trackId, (b) new-track multi-drag via buildConfigFromDragResult + type:'config' \u2014 inject pinnedShotGroups into the resolved config, (c) single-clip moveClipToRow in useTimelineTrackManagement \u2014 needs similar treatment. Read all three paths before coding.\n\n5. **T14 (shot drop)** \u2014 the existing handleAssetDrop is imperative and commits per asset. You MUST extract clip-building logic into a pure function or build clips inline. Do NOT call handleAssetDrop in a loop \u2014 that violates the single-applyEdit requirement.\n\n6. **T13 (shot drag type) has no dependencies** and can start in parallel with Phase 1.\n\n7. **T15 (auto-sync)** needs debouncing. Realtime shot image events can fire rapidly. Consider a 300ms debounce or batching within a single requestAnimationFrame.\n\n8. **Plan has duplicate steps**: Steps 13-14 are TODO placeholders that duplicate Steps 21-24. This finalize maps both sets to the concrete T13/T14/T15 tasks. Ignore the TODO versions.\n\n9. **Test strategy**: Don't create new test files except within existing test files. Add tests to useShotGroups.test.ts and serialize.test.ts. The final validation (T16) runs full video-editor suite + build check.",

        Idea:
Implement two-tier shot groups on the video editor timeline: suggested (inferred, dashed border) and pinned (persistent, solid border).

## Core concept
The current useShotGroups inference becomes 'suggested' groups shown with dashed borders. Users can promote them to 'pinned' groups which are stored in timeline config, persist across refresh, and enable advanced features.

## Data model
PinnedShotGroup stored in timelineConfig:
- shotId, trackId, clipIds[], mode: 'images' | 'video', videoAssetKey?, imageClipSnapshot? (for swap-back)

## When pinned groups are created (explicit + implicit):

### Explicit:
1. Right-click a suggested group → 'Pin as Shot Group' - writes PinnedShotGroup to config
2. Drop a shot from shot list/gallery onto timeline - creates pinned group with images expanded as clips

### Implicit (auto-pin):
3. 'Switch to Final Video' on a suggested group - auto-pins first (snapshots image clips), then swaps to video mode
4. When an image is added to a shot that already has a pinned group on the timeline - auto-inserts the new image clip into the pinned group's track at the right position

## Visual distinction:
- Suggested: dashed border, lighter color (current border style → dashed)
- Pinned: solid border, full color (current styling), shot name visible

## Pinned group behavior:
- Clips drag together as a unit (grouped drag)
- Image ↔ video toggle: switch stores snapshot of image clips, restores on switch-back. Single applyEdit each direction.
- Shot image sync: when images are added/removed from a shot, pinned group auto-updates (subscribe to shot changes via realtime or ShotsContext)
- Context menu: Pin/Unpin, Switch to Video/Images, Jump to Shot, Generate Video

## Key architectural decisions:
- pinnedShotGroups stored in TimelineData (persisted via timeline config, undoable)
- useShotGroups still runs for inference but pinned groups take priority (suppress inferred for same shot+track)
- PinnedShotGroup clipIds are the source of truth for which clips belong to the group
- When a pinned group exists, the shot group overlay reads from the pinned data, not from inference

## Key files to research:
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useShotGroups.ts - current inference
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useSwitchToFinalVideo.ts - current swap (to be replaced)
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts - applyEdit, TimelineEditMutation, timeline config persistence
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts - drag behavior (need grouped drag)
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useExternalDrop.ts - drop from outside (need shot drop)
- src/tools/video-editor/lib/timeline-data.ts - TimelineData type, ClipMeta
- src/tools/video-editor/types/index.ts - AssetRegistry types
- src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.tsx - rendering shot groups
- src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ShotGroupContextMenu.tsx - context menu
- src/shared/contexts/ShotsContext.tsx - shot data, realtime updates
- src/shared/hooks/shots/useShotImages.ts - shot image data
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts - asset registration
- src/tools/video-editor/contexts/TimelineEditorContext.ts - editor context/providers

User notes and answers:
- Addressing critique flags:

FLAG-001 (suppression granularity): Use clipIds-based suppression instead of shotId:trackId. A pinned group stores its clipIds. When filtering inferred groups, suppress any inferred group whose clipIds are a subset of a pinned group's clipIds. This handles multiple clusters of the same shot on one track.

FLAG-002/correctness-2/callers-1 (applyEdit config mutations): Add a new mutation type to TimelineEditMutation: { type: 'pinnedShotGroups', pinnedShotGroups: PinnedShotGroup[] }. This is cleaner than trying to squeeze metadata into the existing config or rows paths. The commit handler reads current data, replaces pinnedShotGroups, and rebuilds. For switch-to-video which needs BOTH rows changes AND pinnedShotGroups changes, use the existing type:'rows' mutation but add an optional pinnedShotGroupsOverride field.

FLAG-003 (grouped drag): Defer group expansion to after drag threshold is crossed, not on pointer-down. On pointer-down, just record that the clip is in a pinned group. On first pointermove past threshold, expand draggedClipIds to include all group clips.

FLAG-004/scope-1/all_locations-3 (shot drop DnD): Add a new drag type 'shot' to shared DnD utilities. Add drag source in shot list components. Add acceptance in onTimelineDragOver. This is Phase 6 and can be a follow-up if needed.

FLAG-005/all_locations-1 (migrateToFlatTracks): Explicitly update migrateToFlatTracks to preserve pinnedShotGroups. It currently rebuilds config with an allowlist - add pinnedShotGroups to that list.

all_locations-2 (rowsToConfig callers): Update render-bounds.validation.test.ts and any other direct callers.

issue_hints-1 (clip lifecycle): When a clip in a pinned group is manually deleted, remove it from the group's clipIds. If clipIds becomes empty, remove the pinned group. If in video mode and the video clip is deleted, auto-switch back to images from snapshot if available, otherwise remove the group.

issue_hints-2 (hasFinalVideo guard): Preserve the existing guard - Switch to Video only shows when finalVideoMap.get(shotId) exists. Switch to Images only shows when mode is video.

conventions-1 (reuse insertion helpers): Reuse useAssetManagement helpers for shot drop clip creation rather than hand-building.

conventions-2 (mutation model): All pinned group changes go through applyEdit, never direct mutation of dataRef.current. This preserves undo/history.

  "meta_commentary": "Execution guidance:\n\n1. **Start with T1+T2 sequentially** \u2014 they're the foundation. Read types/index.ts, serialize.ts, migrate.ts, timeline-data.ts, and useTimelineCommit.ts before making changes. The customEffects pattern is your template.\n\n2. **T3 is the highest-risk task.** The 'rows' branch with pinnedShotGroupsOverride is where critique flags converge. Key insight: after materializeData() produces new data from rows, you MUST set pinnedShotGroups on the resulting config and THEN rebuild TimelineData from it (or ensure assembleTimelineData sees the final config). Post-hoc mutation of an already-assembled TimelineData leaves stableSignature stale. The cleanest approach: materializeData returns a config, apply override to config, then pass to buildDataFromCurrentRegistry.\n\n3. **T10 (clip lifecycle)** is second highest risk. The plan says \"post-commit reconcile\" but that creates double history. Instead: make reconciliation part of materializeData itself. When it rebuilds rows, check if any pinned group clipIds reference clips no longer in the new rows. Clean them in the same data pass, before commitData. Zero extra undo entries.\n\n4. **T12 (grouped drag)** has THREE code paths to handle: (a) same-track multi-drag via type:'rows' \u2014 add pinnedShotGroupsOverride with updated trackId, (b) new-track multi-drag via buildConfigFromDragResult + type:'config' \u2014 inject pinnedShotGroups into the resolved config, (c) single-clip moveClipToRow in useTimelineTrackManagement \u2014 needs similar treatment. Read all three paths before coding.\n\n5. **T14 (shot drop)** \u2014 the existing handleAssetDrop is imperative and commits per asset. You MUST extract clip-building logic into a pure function or build clips inline.         Idea:
Implement two-tier shot groups on the video editor timeline: suggested (inferred, dashed border) and pinned (persistent, solid border).

## Core concept
The current useShotGroups inference becomes 'suggested' groups shown with dashed borders. Users can promote them to 'pinned' groups which are stored in timeline config, persist across refresh, and enable advanced features.

## Data model
PinnedShotGroup stored in timelineConfig:
- shotId, trackId, clipIds[], mode: 'images' | 'video', videoAssetKey?, imageClipSnapshot? (for swap-back)

## When pinned groups are created (explicit + implicit):

### Explicit:
1. Right-click a suggested group → 'Pin as Shot Group' - writes PinnedShotGroup to config
2. Drop a shot from shot list/gallery onto timeline - creates pinned group with images expanded as clips

### Implicit (auto-pin):
3. 'Switch to Final Video' on a suggested group - auto-pins first (snapshots image clips), then swaps to video mode
4. When an image is added to a shot that already has a pinned group on the timeline - auto-inserts the new image clip into the pinned group's track at the right position

## Visual distinction:
- Suggested: dashed border, lighter color (current border style → dashed)
- Pinned: solid border, full color (current styling), shot name visible

## Pinned group behavior:
- Clips drag together as a unit (grouped drag)
- Image ↔ video toggle: switch stores snapshot of image clips, restores on switch-back. Single applyEdit each direction.
- Shot image sync: when images are added/removed from a shot, pinned group auto-updates (subscribe to shot changes via realtime or ShotsContext)
- Context menu: Pin/Unpin, Switch to Video/Images, Jump to Shot, Generate Video

## Key architectural decisions:
- pinnedShotGroups stored in TimelineData (persisted via timeline config, undoable)
- useShotGroups still runs for inference but pinned groups take priority (suppress inferred for same shot+track)
- PinnedShotGroup clipIds are the source of truth for which clips belong to the group
- When a pinned group exists, the shot group overlay reads from the pinned data, not from inference

## Key files to research:
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useShotGroups.ts - current inference
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useSwitchToFinalVideo.ts - current swap (to be replaced)
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts - applyEdit, TimelineEditMutation, timeline config persistence
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts - drag behavior (need grouped drag)
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useExternalDrop.ts - drop from outside (need shot drop)
- src/tools/video-editor/lib/timeline-data.ts - TimelineData type, ClipMeta
- src/tools/video-editor/types/index.ts - AssetRegistry types
- src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.tsx - rendering shot groups
- src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ShotGroupContextMenu.tsx - context menu
- src/shared/contexts/ShotsContext.tsx - shot data, realtime updates
- src/shared/hooks/shots/useShotImages.ts - shot image data
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts - asset registration
- src/tools/video-editor/contexts/TimelineEditorContext.ts - editor context/providers

User notes and answers:
- Addressing critique flags:

FLAG-001 (suppression granularity): Use clipIds-based suppression instead of shotId:trackId. A pinned group stores its clipIds. When filtering inferred groups, suppress any inferred group whose clipIds are a subset of a pinned group's clipIds. This handles multiple clusters of the same shot on one track.

FLAG-002/correctness-2/callers-1 (applyEdit config mutations): Add a new mutation type to TimelineEditMutation: { type: 'pinnedShotGroups', pinnedShotGroups: PinnedShotGroup[] }. This is cleaner than trying to squeeze metadata into the existing config or rows paths. The commit handler reads current data, replaces pinnedShotGroups, and rebuilds. For switch-to-video which needs BOTH rows changes AND pinnedShotGroups changes, use the existing type:'rows' mutation but add an optional pinnedShotGroupsOverride field.

FLAG-003 (grouped drag): Defer group expansion to after drag threshold is crossed, not on pointer-down. On pointer-down, just record that the clip is in a pinned group. On first pointermove past threshold, expand draggedClipIds to include all group clips.

FLAG-004/scope-1/all_locations-3 (shot drop DnD): Add a new drag type 'shot' to shared DnD utilities. Add drag source in shot list components. Add acceptance in onTimelineDragOver. This is Phase 6 and can be a follow-up if needed.

FLAG-005/all_locations-1 (migrateToFlatTracks): Explicitly update migrateToFlatTracks to preserve pinnedShotGroups. It currently rebuilds config with an allowlist - add pinnedShotGroups to that list.

all_locations-2 (rowsToConfig callers): Update render-bounds.validation.test.ts and any other direct callers.

issue_hints-1 (clip lifecycle): When a clip in a pinned group is manually deleted, remove it from the group's clipIds. If clipIds becomes empty, remove the pinned group. If in video mode and the video clip is deleted, auto-switch back to images from snapshot if available, otherwise remove the group.

issue_hints-2 (hasFinalVideo guard): Preserve the existing guard - Switch to Video only shows when finalVideoMap.get(shotId) exists. Switch to Images only shows when mode is video.

conventions-1 (reuse insertion helpers): Reuse useAssetManagement helpers for shot drop clip creation rather than hand-building.

conventions-2 (mutation model): All pinned group changes go through applyEdit, never direct mutation of dataRef.current. This preserves undo/history.

  "meta_commentary": "Execution guidance:\n\n1. **Start with T1+T2 sequentially** \u2014 they're the foundation. Read types/index.ts, serialize.ts, migrate.ts, timeline-data.ts, and useTimelineCommit.ts before making changes. The customEffects pattern is your template.\n\n2. **T3 is the highest-risk task.** The 'rows' branch with pinnedShotGroupsOverride is where critique flags converge. Key insight: after materializeData() produces new data from rows, you MUST set pinnedShotGroups on the resulting config and THEN rebuild TimelineData from it (or ensure assembleTimelineData sees the final config). Post-hoc mutation of an already-assembled TimelineData leaves stableSignature stale. The cleanest approach: materializeData returns a config, apply override to config, then pass to buildDataFromCurrentRegistry.\n\n3. **T10 (clip lifecycle)** is second highest risk. The plan says \"post-commit reconcile\" but that creates double history. Instead: make reconciliation part of materializeData itself. When it rebuilds rows, check if any pinned group clipIds reference clips no longer in the new rows. Clean them in the same data pass, before commitData. Zero extra undo entries.\n\n4. **T12 (grouped drag)** has THREE code paths to handle: (a) same-track multi-drag via type:'rows' \u2014 add pinnedShotGroupsOverride with updated trackId, (b) new-track multi-drag via buildConfigFromDragResult + type:'config' \u2014 inject pinnedShotGroups into the resolved config, (c) single-clip moveClipToRow in useTimelineTrackManagement \u2014 needs similar treatment. Read all three paths before coding.\n\n5. **T14 (shot drop)** \u2014 the existing handleAssetDrop is imperative and commits per asset. You MUST extract clip-building logic into a pure function or build clips inline. Do NOT call handleAssetDrop in a loop \u2014 that violates the single-applyEdit requirement.\n\n6. **T13 (shot drag type) has no dependencies** and can start in parallel with Phase 1.\n\n7. **T15 (auto-sync)** needs debouncing. Realtime shot image events can fire rapidly.         Idea:
Implement two-tier shot groups on the video editor timeline: suggested (inferred, dashed border) and pinned (persistent, solid border).

## Core concept
The current useShotGroups inference becomes 'suggested' groups shown with dashed borders. Users can promote them to 'pinned' groups which are stored in timeline config, persist across refresh, and enable advanced features.

## Data model
PinnedShotGroup stored in timelineConfig:
- shotId, trackId, clipIds[], mode: 'images' | 'video', videoAssetKey?, imageClipSnapshot? (for swap-back)

## When pinned groups are created (explicit + implicit):

### Explicit:
1. Right-click a suggested group → 'Pin as Shot Group' - writes PinnedShotGroup to config
2. Drop a shot from shot list/gallery onto timeline - creates pinned group with images expanded as clips

### Implicit (auto-pin):
3. 'Switch to Final Video' on a suggested group - auto-pins first (snapshots image clips), then swaps to video mode
4. When an image is added to a shot that already has a pinned group on the timeline - auto-inserts the new image clip into the pinned group's track at the right position

## Visual distinction:
- Suggested: dashed border, lighter color (current border style → dashed)
- Pinned: solid border, full color (current styling), shot name visible

## Pinned group behavior:
- Clips drag together as a unit (grouped drag)
- Image ↔ video toggle: switch stores snapshot of image clips, restores on switch-back. Single applyEdit each direction.
- Shot image sync: when images are added/removed from a shot, pinned group auto-updates (subscribe to shot changes via realtime or ShotsContext)
- Context menu: Pin/Unpin, Switch to Video/Images, Jump to Shot, Generate Video

## Key architectural decisions:
- pinnedShotGroups stored in TimelineData (persisted via timeline config, undoable)
- useShotGroups still runs for inference but pinned groups take priority (suppress inferred for same shot+track)
- PinnedShotGroup clipIds are the source of truth for which clips belong to the group
- When a pinned group exists, the shot group overlay reads from the pinned data, not from inference

## Key files to research:
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useShotGroups.ts - current inference
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useSwitchToFinalVideo.ts - current swap (to be replaced)
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts - applyEdit, TimelineEditMutation, timeline config persistence
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts - drag behavior (need grouped drag)
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useExternalDrop.ts - drop from outside (need shot drop)
- src/tools/video-editor/lib/timeline-data.ts - TimelineData type, ClipMeta
- src/tools/video-editor/types/index.ts - AssetRegistry types
- src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.tsx - rendering shot groups
- src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ShotGroupContextMenu.tsx - context menu
- src/shared/contexts/ShotsContext.tsx - shot data, realtime updates
- src/shared/hooks/shots/useShotImages.ts - shot image data
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts - asset registration
- src/tools/video-editor/contexts/TimelineEditorContext.ts - editor context/providers

User notes and answers:
- Addressing critique flags:

FLAG-001 (suppression granularity): Use clipIds-based suppression instead of shotId:trackId. A pinned group stores its clipIds. When filtering inferred groups, suppress any inferred group whose clipIds are a subset of a pinned group's clipIds. This handles multiple clusters of the same shot on one track.

FLAG-002/correctness-2/callers-1 (applyEdit config mutations): Add a new mutation type to TimelineEditMutation: { type: 'pinnedShotGroups', pinnedShotGroups: PinnedShotGroup[] }. This is cleaner than trying to squeeze metadata into the existing config or rows paths. The commit handler reads current data, replaces pinnedShotGroups, and rebuilds. For switch-to-video which needs BOTH rows changes AND pinnedShotGroups changes, use the existing type:'rows' mutation but add an optional pinnedShotGroupsOverride field.

FLAG-003 (grouped drag): Defer group expansion to after drag threshold is crossed, not on pointer-down. On pointer-down, just record that the clip is in a pinned group. On first pointermove past threshold, expand draggedClipIds to include all group clips.

FLAG-004/scope-1/all_locations-3 (shot drop DnD): Add a new drag type 'shot' to shared DnD utilities. Add drag source in shot list components. Add acceptance in onTimelineDragOver. This is Phase 6 and can be a follow-up if needed.

FLAG-005/all_locations-1 (migrateToFlatTracks): Explicitly update migrateToFlatTracks to preserve pinnedShotGroups. It currently rebuilds config with an allowlist - add pinnedShotGroups to that list.

all_locations-2 (rowsToConfig callers): Update render-bounds.validation.test.ts and any other direct callers.

issue_hints-1 (clip lifecycle): When a clip in a pinned group is manually deleted, remove it from the group's clipIds. If clipIds becomes empty, remove the pinned group. If in video mode and the video clip is deleted, auto-switch back to images from snapshot if available, otherwise remove the group.

issue_hints-2 (hasFinalVideo guard): Preserve the existing guard - Switch to Video only shows when finalVideoMap.get(shotId) exists. Switch to Images only shows when mode is video.

conventions-1 (reuse insertion helpers): Reuse useAssetManagement helpers for shot drop clip creation rather than hand-building.

conventions-2 (mutation model): All pinned group changes go through applyEdit, never direct mutation of dataRef.current. This preserves undo/history.

  "meta_commentary": "Execution guidance:\n\n1. **Start with T1+T2 sequentially** \u2014 they're the foundation. Read types/index.ts, serialize.ts, migrate.ts, timeline-data.ts, and useTimelineCommit.ts before making changes. The customEffects pattern is your template.\n\n2. **T3 is the highest-risk task.** The 'rows' branch with pinnedShotGroupsOverride is where critique flags converge. Key insight: after materializeData() produces new data from rows, you MUST set pinnedShotGroups on the resulting config and THEN rebuild TimelineData from it (or ensure assembleTimelineData sees the final config). Post-hoc mutation of an already-assembled TimelineData leaves stableSignature stale. The cleanest approach: materializeData returns a config, apply override to config, then pass to buildDataFromCurrentRegistry.\n\n3. **T10 (clip lifecycle)** is second highest risk. The plan says \"post-commit reconcile\" but that creates double history. Instead: make reconciliation part of materializeData itself. When it rebuilds rows, check if any pinned group clipIds reference clips no longer in the new rows. Clean them in the same data pass, before commitData. Zero extra undo entries.\n\n4. **T12 (grouped drag)** has THREE code paths to handle: (a) same-track multi-drag via type:'rows' \u2014 add pinnedShotGroupsOverride with updated trackId, (b) new-track multi-drag via buildConfigFromDragResult + type:'config' \u2014 inject pinnedShotGroups into the resolved config, (c) single-clip moveClipToRow in useTimelineTrackManagement \u2014 needs similar treatment. Read all three paths before coding.\n\n5. **T14 (shot drop)** \u2014 the existing handleAssetDrop is imperative and commits per asset. You MUST extract clip-building logic into a pure function or build clips inline. Do NOT call handleAssetDrop in a loop \u2014 that violates the single-applyEdit requirement.\n\n6. **T13 (shot drag type) has no dependencies** and can start in parallel with Phase 1.\n\n7. **T15 (auto-sync)** needs debouncing. Realtime shot image events can fire rapidly. Consider a 300ms debounce or batching within a single requestAnimationFrame.\n\n8. **Plan has duplicate steps**: Steps 13-14 are TODO placeholders that duplicate Steps 21-24. This finalize maps both sets to the concrete T13/T14/T15 tasks. Ignore the TODO versions.\n\n9. **Test strategy**: Don't create new test files except within existing test files.         Idea:
Implement two-tier shot groups on the video editor timeline: suggested (inferred, dashed border) and pinned (persistent, solid border).

## Core concept
The current useShotGroups inference becomes 'suggested' groups shown with dashed borders. Users can promote them to 'pinned' groups which are stored in timeline config, persist across refresh, and enable advanced features.

## Data model
PinnedShotGroup stored in timelineConfig:
- shotId, trackId, clipIds[], mode: 'images' | 'video', videoAssetKey?, imageClipSnapshot? (for swap-back)

## When pinned groups are created (explicit + implicit):

### Explicit:
1. Right-click a suggested group → 'Pin as Shot Group' - writes PinnedShotGroup to config
2. Drop a shot from shot list/gallery onto timeline - creates pinned group with images expanded as clips

### Implicit (auto-pin):
3. 'Switch to Final Video' on a suggested group - auto-pins first (snapshots image clips), then swaps to video mode
4. When an image is added to a shot that already has a pinned group on the timeline - auto-inserts the new image clip into the pinned group's track at the right position

## Visual distinction:
- Suggested: dashed border, lighter color (current border style → dashed)
- Pinned: solid border, full color (current styling), shot name visible

## Pinned group behavior:
- Clips drag together as a unit (grouped drag)
- Image ↔ video toggle: switch stores snapshot of image clips, restores on switch-back. Single applyEdit each direction.
- Shot image sync: when images are added/removed from a shot, pinned group auto-updates (subscribe to shot changes via realtime or ShotsContext)
- Context menu: Pin/Unpin, Switch to Video/Images, Jump to Shot, Generate Video

## Key architectural decisions:
- pinnedShotGroups stored in TimelineData (persisted via timeline config, undoable)
- useShotGroups still runs for inference but pinned groups take priority (suppress inferred for same shot+track)
- PinnedShotGroup clipIds are the source of truth for which clips belong to the group
- When a pinned group exists, the shot group overlay reads from the pinned data, not from inference

## Key files to research:
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useShotGroups.ts - current inference
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useSwitchToFinalVideo.ts - current swap (to be replaced)
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts - applyEdit, TimelineEditMutation, timeline config persistence
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts - drag behavior (need grouped drag)
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useExternalDrop.ts - drop from outside (need shot drop)
- src/tools/video-editor/lib/timeline-data.ts - TimelineData type, ClipMeta
- src/tools/video-editor/types/index.ts - AssetRegistry types
- src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.tsx - rendering shot groups
- src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ShotGroupContextMenu.tsx - context menu
- src/shared/contexts/ShotsContext.tsx - shot data, realtime updates
- src/shared/hooks/shots/useShotImages.ts - shot image data
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts - asset registration
- src/tools/video-editor/contexts/TimelineEditorContext.ts - editor context/providers

User notes and answers:
- Addressing critique flags:

FLAG-001 (suppression granularity): Use clipIds-based suppression instead of shotId:trackId. A pinned group stores its clipIds. When filtering inferred groups, suppress any inferred group whose clipIds are a subset of a pinned group's clipIds. This handles multiple clusters of the same shot on one track.

FLAG-002/correctness-2/callers-1 (applyEdit config mutations): Add a new mutation type to TimelineEditMutation: { type: 'pinnedShotGroups', pinnedShotGroups: PinnedShotGroup[] }. This is cleaner than trying to squeeze metadata into the existing config or rows paths. The commit handler reads current data, replaces pinnedShotGroups, and rebuilds. For switch-to-video which needs BOTH rows changes AND pinnedShotGroups changes, use the existing type:'rows' mutation but add an optional pinnedShotGroupsOverride field.

FLAG-003 (grouped drag): Defer group expansion to after drag threshold is crossed, not on pointer-down. On pointer-down, just record that the clip is in a pinned group. On first pointermove past threshold, expand draggedClipIds to include all group clips.

FLAG-004/scope-1/all_locations-3 (shot drop DnD): Add a new drag type 'shot' to shared DnD utilities. Add drag source in shot list components. Add acceptance in onTimelineDragOver. This is Phase 6 and can be a follow-up if needed.

FLAG-005/all_locations-1 (migrateToFlatTracks): Explicitly update migrateToFlatTracks to preserve pinnedShotGroups. It currently rebuilds config with an allowlist - add pinnedShotGroups to that list.

all_locations-2 (rowsToConfig callers): Update render-bounds.validation.test.ts and any other direct callers.

issue_hints-1 (clip lifecycle): When a clip in a pinned group is manually deleted, remove it from the group's clipIds. If clipIds becomes empty, remove the pinned group. If in video mode and the video clip is deleted, auto-switch back to images from snapshot if available, otherwise remove the group.

issue_hints-2 (hasFinalVideo guard): Preserve the existing guard - Switch to Video only shows when finalVideoMap.get(shotId) exists. Switch to Images only shows when mode is video.

conventions-1 (reuse insertion helpers): Reuse useAssetManagement helpers for shot drop clip creation rather than hand-building.

conventions-2 (mutation model): All pinned group changes go through applyEdit, never direct mutation of dataRef.current. This preserves undo/history.

  "meta_commentary": "Execution guidance:\n\n1. **Start with T1+T2 sequentially** \u2014 they're the foundation. Read types/index.ts, serialize.ts, migrate.ts, timeline-data.ts, and useTimelineCommit.ts before making changes. The customEffects pattern is your template.\n\n2. **T3 is the highest-risk task.** The 'rows' branch with pinnedShotGroupsOverride is where critique flags converge. Key insight: after materializeData() produces new data from rows, you MUST set pinnedShotGroups on the resulting config and THEN rebuild TimelineData from it (or ensure assembleTimelineData sees the final config). Post-hoc mutation of an already-assembled TimelineData leaves stableSignature stale. The cleanest approach: materializeData returns a config, apply override to config, then pass to buildDataFromCurrentRegistry.\n\n3. **T10 (clip lifecycle)** is second highest risk. The plan says \"post-commit reconcile\" but that creates double history. Instead: make reconciliation part of materializeData itself. When it rebuilds rows, check if any pinned group clipIds reference clips no longer in the new rows. Clean them in the same data pass, before commitData. Zero extra undo entries.\n\n4. **T12 (grouped drag)** has THREE code paths to handle: (a) same-track multi-drag via type:'rows' \u2014 add pinnedShotGroupsOverride with updated trackId, (b) new-track multi-drag via buildConfigFromDragResult + type:'config' \u2014 inject pinnedShotGroups into the resolved config, (c) single-clip moveClipToRow in useTimelineTrackManagement \u2014 needs similar treatment. Read all three paths before coding.\n\n5. **T14 (shot drop)** \u2014 the existing handleAssetDrop is imperative and commits per asset. You MUST extract clip-building logic into a pure function or build clips inline. Do NOT call handleAssetDrop in a loop \u2014 that violates the single-applyEdit requirement.\n\n6. **T13 (shot drag type) has no dependencies** and can start in parallel with Phase 1.\n\n7. **T15 (auto-sync)** needs debouncing. Realtime shot image events can fire rapidly. Consider a 300ms debounce or batching within a single requestAnimationFrame.\n\n8. **Plan has duplicate steps**: Steps 13-14 are TODO placeholders that duplicate Steps 21-24. This finalize maps both sets to the concrete T13/T14/T15 tasks. Ignore the TODO versions.\n\n9. **Test strategy**: Don't create new test files except within existing test files.         Idea:
Implement two-tier shot groups on the video editor timeline: suggested (inferred, dashed border) and pinned (persistent, solid border).

## Core concept
The current useShotGroups inference becomes 'suggested' groups shown with dashed borders. Users can promote them to 'pinned' groups which are stored in timeline config, persist across refresh, and enable advanced features.

## Data model
PinnedShotGroup stored in timelineConfig:
- shotId, trackId, clipIds[], mode: 'images' | 'video', videoAssetKey?, imageClipSnapshot? (for swap-back)

## When pinned groups are created (explicit + implicit):

### Explicit:
1. Right-click a suggested group → 'Pin as Shot Group' - writes PinnedShotGroup to config
2. Drop a shot from shot list/gallery onto timeline - creates pinned group with images expanded as clips

### Implicit (auto-pin):
3. 'Switch to Final Video' on a suggested group - auto-pins first (snapshots image clips), then swaps to video mode
4. When an image is added to a shot that already has a pinned group on the timeline - auto-inserts the new image clip into the pinned group's track at the right position

## Visual distinction:
- Suggested: dashed border, lighter color (current border style → dashed)
- Pinned: solid border, full color (current styling), shot name visible

## Pinned group behavior:
- Clips drag together as a unit (grouped drag)
- Image ↔ video toggle: switch stores snapshot of image clips, restores on switch-back. Single applyEdit each direction.
- Shot image sync: when images are added/removed from a shot, pinned group auto-updates (subscribe to shot changes via realtime or ShotsContext)
- Context menu: Pin/Unpin, Switch to Video/Images, Jump to Shot, Generate Video

## Key architectural decisions:
- pinnedShotGroups stored in TimelineData (persisted via timeline config, undoable)
- useShotGroups still runs for inference but pinned groups take priority (suppress inferred for same shot+track)
- PinnedShotGroup clipIds are the source of truth for which clips belong to the group
- When a pinned group exists, the shot group overlay reads from the pinned data, not from inference

## Key files to research:
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useShotGroups.ts - current inference
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useSwitchToFinalVideo.ts - current swap (to be replaced)
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts - applyEdit, TimelineEditMutation, timeline config persistence
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts - drag behavior (need grouped drag)
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useExternalDrop.ts - drop from outside (need shot drop)
- src/tools/video-editor/lib/timeline-data.ts - TimelineData type, ClipMeta
- src/tools/video-editor/types/index.ts - AssetRegistry types
- src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.tsx - rendering shot groups
- src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ShotGroupContextMenu.tsx - context menu
- src/shared/contexts/ShotsContext.tsx - shot data, realtime updates
- src/shared/hooks/shots/useShotImages.ts - shot image data
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts - asset registration
- src/tools/video-editor/contexts/TimelineEditorContext.ts - editor context/providers

User notes and answers:
- Addressing critique flags:

FLAG-001 (suppression granularity): Use clipIds-based suppression instead of shotId:trackId. A pinned group stores its clipIds. When filtering inferred groups, suppress any inferred group whose clipIds are a subset of a pinned group's clipIds. This handles multiple clusters of the same shot on one track.

FLAG-002/correctness-2/callers-1 (applyEdit config mutations): Add a new mutation type to TimelineEditMutation: { type: 'pinnedShotGroups', pinnedShotGroups: PinnedShotGroup[] }. This is cleaner than trying to squeeze metadata into the existing config or rows paths. The commit handler reads current data, replaces pinnedShotGroups, and rebuilds. For switch-to-video which needs BOTH rows changes AND pinnedShotGroups changes, use the existing type:'rows' mutation but add an optional pinnedShotGroupsOverride field.

FLAG-003 (grouped drag): Defer group expansion to after drag threshold is crossed, not on pointer-down. On pointer-down, just record that the clip is in a pinned group. On first pointermove past threshold, expand draggedClipIds to include all group clips.

FLAG-004/scope-1/all_locations-3 (shot drop DnD): Add a new drag type 'shot' to shared DnD utilities. Add drag source in shot list components. Add acceptance in onTimelineDragOver. This is Phase 6 and can be a follow-up if needed.

FLAG-005/all_locations-1 (migrateToFlatTracks): Explicitly update migrateToFlatTracks to preserve pinnedShotGroups. It currently rebuilds config with an allowlist - add pinnedShotGroups to that list.

all_locations-2 (rowsToConfig callers): Update render-bounds.validation.test.ts and any other direct callers.

issue_hints-1 (clip lifecycle): When a clip in a pinned group is manually deleted, remove it from the group's clipIds. If clipIds becomes empty, remove the pinned group. If in video mode and the video clip is deleted, auto-switch back to images from snapshot if available, otherwise remove the group.

issue_hints-2 (hasFinalVideo guard): Preserve the existing guard - Switch to Video only shows when finalVideoMap.get(shotId) exists. Switch to Images only shows when mode is video.

conventions-1 (reuse insertion helpers): Reuse useAssetManagement helpers for shot drop clip creation rather than hand-building.

conventions-2 (mutation model): All pinned group changes go through applyEdit, never direct mutation of dataRef.current. This preserves undo/history.

The customEffects pattern is your template.\n\n2. **T3 is the highest-risk task.** The 'rows' branch with pinnedShotGroupsOverride is where critique flags converge. Key insight: after materializeData() produces new data from rows, you MUST set pinnedShotGroups on the resulting config and THEN rebuild TimelineData from it (or ensure assembleTimelineData sees the final config). Post-hoc mutation of an already-assembled TimelineData leaves stableSignature stale. The cleanest approach: materializeData returns a config, apply override to config, then pass to buildDataFromCurrentRegistry.\n\n3. **T10 (clip lifecycle)** is second highest risk. The plan says \"post-commit reconcile\" but that creates double history. Instead: make reconciliation part of materializeData itself. When it rebuilds rows, check if any pinned group clipIds reference clips no longer in the new rows. Clean them in the same data pass, before commitData. Zero extra undo entries.\n\n4. **T12 (grouped drag)** has THREE code paths to handle: (a) same-track multi-drag via type:'rows' \u2014 add pinnedShotGroupsOverride with updated trackId, (b) new-track multi-drag via buildConfigFromDragResult + type:'config' \u2014 inject pinnedShotGroups into the resolved config, (c) single-clip moveClipToRow in useTimelineTrackManagement \u2014 needs similar treatment. Read all three paths before coding.\n\n5. **T14 (shot drop)** \u2014 the existing handleAssetDrop is imperative and commits per asset. You MUST extract clip-building logic into a pure function or build clips inline. Realtime shot image events can fire rapidly.         Idea:
Implement two-tier shot groups on the video editor timeline: suggested (inferred, dashed border) and pinned (persistent, solid border).

## Core concept
The current useShotGroups inference becomes 'suggested' groups shown with dashed borders. Users can promote them to 'pinned' groups which are stored in timeline config, persist across refresh, and enable advanced features.

## Data model
PinnedShotGroup stored in timelineConfig:
- shotId, trackId, clipIds[], mode: 'images' | 'video', videoAssetKey?, imageClipSnapshot? (for swap-back)

## When pinned groups are created (explicit + implicit):

### Explicit:
1. Right-click a suggested group → 'Pin as Shot Group' - writes PinnedShotGroup to config
2. Drop a shot from shot list/gallery onto timeline - creates pinned group with images expanded as clips

### Implicit (auto-pin):
3. 'Switch to Final Video' on a suggested group - auto-pins first (snapshots image clips), then swaps to video mode
4. When an image is added to a shot that already has a pinned group on the timeline - auto-inserts the new image clip into the pinned group's track at the right position

## Visual distinction:
- Suggested: dashed border, lighter color (current border style → dashed)
- Pinned: solid border, full color (current styling), shot name visible

## Pinned group behavior:
- Clips drag together as a unit (grouped drag)
- Image ↔ video toggle: switch stores snapshot of image clips, restores on switch-back. Single applyEdit each direction.
- Shot image sync: when images are added/removed from a shot, pinned group auto-updates (subscribe to shot changes via realtime or ShotsContext)
- Context menu: Pin/Unpin, Switch to Video/Images, Jump to Shot, Generate Video

## Key architectural decisions:
- pinnedShotGroups stored in TimelineData (persisted via timeline config, undoable)
- useShotGroups still runs for inference but pinned groups take priority (suppress inferred for same shot+track)
- PinnedShotGroup clipIds are the source of truth for which clips belong to the group
- When a pinned group exists, the shot group overlay reads from the pinned data, not from inference

## Key files to research:
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useShotGroups.ts - current inference
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useSwitchToFinalVideo.ts - current swap (to be replaced)
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts - applyEdit, TimelineEditMutation, timeline config persistence
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts - drag behavior (need grouped drag)
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useExternalDrop.ts - drop from outside (need shot drop)
- src/tools/video-editor/lib/timeline-data.ts - TimelineData type, ClipMeta
- src/tools/video-editor/types/index.ts - AssetRegistry types
- src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.tsx - rendering shot groups
- src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ShotGroupContextMenu.tsx - context menu
- src/shared/contexts/ShotsContext.tsx - shot data, realtime updates
- src/shared/hooks/shots/useShotImages.ts - shot image data
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts - asset registration
- src/tools/video-editor/contexts/TimelineEditorContext.ts - editor context/providers

User notes and answers:
- Addressing critique flags:

FLAG-001 (suppression granularity): Use clipIds-based suppression instead of shotId:trackId. A pinned group stores its clipIds. When filtering inferred groups, suppress any inferred group whose clipIds are a subset of a pinned group's clipIds. This handles multiple clusters of the same shot on one track.

FLAG-002/correctness-2/callers-1 (applyEdit config mutations): Add a new mutation type to TimelineEditMutation: { type: 'pinnedShotGroups', pinnedShotGroups: PinnedShotGroup[] }. This is cleaner than trying to squeeze metadata into the existing config or rows paths. The commit handler reads current data, replaces pinnedShotGroups, and rebuilds. For switch-to-video which needs BOTH rows changes AND pinnedShotGroups changes, use the existing type:'rows' mutation but add an optional pinnedShotGroupsOverride field.

FLAG-003 (grouped drag): Defer group expansion to after drag threshold is crossed, not on pointer-down. On pointer-down, just record that the clip is in a pinned group. On first pointermove past threshold, expand draggedClipIds to include all group clips.

FLAG-004/scope-1/all_locations-3 (shot drop DnD): Add a new drag type 'shot' to shared DnD utilities. Add drag source in shot list components. Add acceptance in onTimelineDragOver. This is Phase 6 and can be a follow-up if needed.

FLAG-005/all_locations-1 (migrateToFlatTracks): Explicitly update migrateToFlatTracks to preserve pinnedShotGroups. It currently rebuilds config with an allowlist - add pinnedShotGroups to that list.

all_locations-2 (rowsToConfig callers): Update render-bounds.validation.test.ts and any other direct callers.

issue_hints-1 (clip lifecycle): When a clip in a pinned group is manually deleted, remove it from the group's clipIds. If clipIds becomes empty, remove the pinned group. If in video mode and the video clip is deleted, auto-switch back to images from snapshot if available, otherwise remove the group.

issue_hints-2 (hasFinalVideo guard): Preserve the existing guard - Switch to Video only shows when finalVideoMap.get(shotId) exists. Switch to Images only shows when mode is video.

conventions-1 (reuse insertion helpers): Reuse useAssetManagement helpers for shot drop clip creation rather than hand-building.

conventions-2 (mutation model): All pinned group changes go through applyEdit, never direct mutation of dataRef.current. This preserves undo/history.

        Idea:
Implement two-tier shot groups on the video editor timeline: suggested (inferred, dashed border) and pinned (persistent, solid border).

## Core concept
The current useShotGroups inference becomes 'suggested' groups shown with dashed borders. Users can promote them to 'pinned' groups which are stored in timeline config, persist across refresh, and enable advanced features.

## Data model
PinnedShotGroup stored in timelineConfig:
- shotId, trackId, clipIds[], mode: 'images' | 'video', videoAssetKey?, imageClipSnapshot? (for swap-back)

## When pinned groups are created (explicit + implicit):

### Explicit:
1. Right-click a suggested group → 'Pin as Shot Group' - writes PinnedShotGroup to config
2. Drop a shot from shot list/gallery onto timeline - creates pinned group with images expanded as clips

### Implicit (auto-pin):
3. 'Switch to Final Video' on a suggested group - auto-pins first (snapshots image clips), then swaps to video mode
4. When an image is added to a shot that already has a pinned group on the timeline - auto-inserts the new image clip into the pinned group's track at the right position

## Visual distinction:
- Suggested: dashed border, lighter color (current border style → dashed)
- Pinned: solid border, full color (current styling), shot name visible

## Pinned group behavior:
- Clips drag together as a unit (grouped drag)
- Image ↔ video toggle: switch stores snapshot of image clips, restores on switch-back. Single applyEdit each direction.
- Shot image sync: when images are added/removed from a shot, pinned group auto-updates (subscribe to shot changes via realtime or ShotsContext)
- Context menu: Pin/Unpin, Switch to Video/Images, Jump to Shot, Generate Video

## Key architectural decisions:
- pinnedShotGroups stored in TimelineData (persisted via timeline config, undoable)
- useShotGroups still runs for inference but pinned groups take priority (suppress inferred for same shot+track)
- PinnedShotGroup clipIds are the source of truth for which clips belong to the group
- When a pinned group exists, the shot group overlay reads from the pinned data, not from inference

## Key files to research:
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useShotGroups.ts - current inference
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useSwitchToFinalVideo.ts - current swap (to be replaced)
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts - applyEdit, TimelineEditMutation, timeline config persistence
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts - drag behavior (need grouped drag)
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useExternalDrop.ts - drop from outside (need shot drop)
- src/tools/video-editor/lib/timeline-data.ts - TimelineData type, ClipMeta
- src/tools/video-editor/types/index.ts - AssetRegistry types
- src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.tsx - rendering shot groups
- src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ShotGroupContextMenu.tsx - context menu
- src/shared/contexts/ShotsContext.tsx - shot data, realtime updates
- src/shared/hooks/shots/useShotImages.ts - shot image data
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts - asset registration
- src/tools/video-editor/contexts/TimelineEditorContext.ts - editor context/providers

User notes and answers:
- Addressing critique flags:

FLAG-001 (suppression granularity): Use clipIds-based suppression instead of shotId:trackId. A pinned group stores its clipIds. When filtering inferred groups, suppress any inferred group whose clipIds are a subset of a pinned group's clipIds. This handles multiple clusters of the same shot on one track.

FLAG-002/correctness-2/callers-1 (applyEdit config mutations): Add a new mutation type to TimelineEditMutation: { type: 'pinnedShotGroups', pinnedShotGroups: PinnedShotGroup[] }. This is cleaner than trying to squeeze metadata into the existing config or rows paths. The commit handler reads current data, replaces pinnedShotGroups, and rebuilds. For switch-to-video which needs BOTH rows changes AND pinnedShotGroups changes, use the existing type:'rows' mutation but add an optional pinnedShotGroupsOverride field.

FLAG-003 (grouped drag): Defer group expansion to after drag threshold is crossed, not on pointer-down. On pointer-down, just record that the clip is in a pinned group. On first pointermove past threshold, expand draggedClipIds to include all group clips.

FLAG-004/scope-1/all_locations-3 (shot drop DnD): Add a new drag type 'shot' to shared DnD utilities. Add drag source in shot list components. Add acceptance in onTimelineDragOver. This is Phase 6 and can be a follow-up if needed.

FLAG-005/all_locations-1 (migrateToFlatTracks): Explicitly update migrateToFlatTracks to preserve pinnedShotGroups. It currently rebuilds config with an allowlist - add pinnedShotGroups to that list.

all_locations-2 (rowsToConfig callers): Update render-bounds.validation.test.ts and any other direct callers.

issue_hints-1 (clip lifecycle): When a clip in a pinned group is manually deleted, remove it from the group's clipIds. If clipIds becomes empty, remove the pinned group. If in video mode and the video clip is deleted, auto-switch back to images from snapshot if available, otherwise remove the group.

issue_hints-2 (hasFinalVideo guard): Preserve the existing guard - Switch to Video only shows when finalVideoMap.get(shotId) exists. Switch to Images only shows when mode is video.

conventions-1 (reuse insertion helpers): Reuse useAssetManagement helpers for shot drop clip creation rather than hand-building.

conventions-2 (mutation model): All pinned group changes go through applyEdit, never direct mutation of dataRef.current. This preserves undo/history.

        Idea:
Implement two-tier shot groups on the video editor timeline: suggested (inferred, dashed border) and pinned (persistent, solid border).

## Core concept
The current useShotGroups inference becomes 'suggested' groups shown with dashed borders. Users can promote them to 'pinned' groups which are stored in timeline config, persist across refresh, and enable advanced features.

## Data model
PinnedShotGroup stored in timelineConfig:
- shotId, trackId, clipIds[], mode: 'images' | 'video', videoAssetKey?, imageClipSnapshot? (for swap-back)

## When pinned groups are created (explicit + implicit):

### Explicit:
1. Right-click a suggested group → 'Pin as Shot Group' - writes PinnedShotGroup to config
2. Drop a shot from shot list/gallery onto timeline - creates pinned group with images expanded as clips

### Implicit (auto-pin):
3. 'Switch to Final Video' on a suggested group - auto-pins first (snapshots image clips), then swaps to video mode
4. When an image is added to a shot that already has a pinned group on the timeline - auto-inserts the new image clip into the pinned group's track at the right position

## Visual distinction:
- Suggested: dashed border, lighter color (current border style → dashed)
- Pinned: solid border, full color (current styling), shot name visible

## Pinned group behavior:
- Clips drag together as a unit (grouped drag)
- Image ↔ video toggle: switch stores snapshot of image clips, restores on switch-back. Single applyEdit each direction.
- Shot image sync: when images are added/removed from a shot, pinned group auto-updates (subscribe to shot changes via realtime or ShotsContext)
- Context menu: Pin/Unpin, Switch to Video/Images, Jump to Shot, Generate Video

## Key architectural decisions:
- pinnedShotGroups stored in TimelineData (persisted via timeline config, undoable)
- useShotGroups still runs for inference but pinned groups take priority (suppress inferred for same shot+track)
- PinnedShotGroup clipIds are the source of truth for which clips belong to the group
- When a pinned group exists, the shot group overlay reads from the pinned data, not from inference

## Key files to research:
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useShotGroups.ts - current inference
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useSwitchToFinalVideo.ts - current swap (to be replaced)
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useTimelineCommit.ts - applyEdit, TimelineEditMutation, timeline config persistence
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useClipDrag.ts - drag behavior (need grouped drag)
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useExternalDrop.ts - drop from outside (need shot drop)
- src/tools/video-editor/lib/timeline-data.ts - TimelineData type, ClipMeta
- src/tools/video-editor/types/index.ts - AssetRegistry types
- src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/TimelineCanvas.tsx - rendering shot groups
- src/tools/video-editor/components/TimelineEditor/ShotGroupContextMenu.tsx - context menu
- src/shared/contexts/ShotsContext.tsx - shot data, realtime updates
- src/shared/hooks/shots/useShotImages.ts - shot image data
- src/tools/video-editor/hooks/useAssetManagement.ts - asset registration
- src/tools/video-editor/contexts/TimelineEditorContext.ts - editor context/providers

User notes and answers:
- Addressing critique flags:

FLAG-001 (suppression granularity): Use clipIds-based suppression instead of shotId:trackId. A pinned group stores its clipIds. When filtering inferred groups, suppress any inferred group whose clipIds are a subset of a pinned group's clipIds. This handles multiple clusters of the same shot on one track.

FLAG-002/correctness-2/callers-1 (applyEdit config mutations): Add a new mutation type to TimelineEditMutation: { type: 'pinnedShotGroups', pinnedShotGroups: PinnedShotGroup[] }. This is cleaner than trying to squeeze metadata into the existing config or rows paths. The commit handler reads current data, replaces pinnedShotGroups, and rebuilds. For switch-to-video which needs BOTH rows changes AND pinnedShotGroups changes, use the existing type:'rows' mutation but add an optional pinnedShotGroupsOverride field.

FLAG-003 (grouped drag): Defer group expansion to after drag threshold is crossed, not on pointer-down. On pointer-down, just record that the clip is in a pinned group. On first pointermove past threshold, expand draggedClipIds to include all group clips.

FLAG-004/scope-1/all_locations-3 (shot drop DnD): Add a new drag type 'shot' to shared DnD utilities. Add drag source in shot list components. Add acceptance in onTimelineDragOver. This is Phase 6 and can be a follow-up if needed.

FLAG-005/all_locations-1 (migrateToFlatTracks): Explicitly update migrateToFlatTracks to preserve pinnedShotGroups. It currently rebuilds config with an allowlist - add pinnedShotGroups to that list.

all_locations-2 (rowsToConfig callers): Update render-bounds.validation.test.ts and any other direct callers.

issue_hints-1 (clip lifecycle): When a clip in a pinned group is manually deleted, remove it from the group's clipIds. If clipIds becomes empty, remove the pinned group. If in video mode and the video clip is deleted, auto-switch back to images from snapshot if available, otherwise remove the group.

issue_hints-2 (hasFinalVideo guard): Preserve the existing guard - Switch to Video only shows when finalVideoMap.get(shotId) exists. Switch to Images only shows when mode is video.

conventions-1 (reuse insertion helpers): Reuse useAssetManagement helpers for shot drop clip creation rather than hand-building.

conventions-2 (mutation model): All pinned group changes go through applyEdit, never direct mutation of dataRef.current. This preserves undo/history.

The customEffects pattern is your template.\n\n2. **T3 is the highest-risk task.** The 'rows' branch with pinnedShotGroupsOverride is where critique flags converge. Key insight: after materializeData() produces new data from rows, you MUST set pinnedShotGroups on the resulting config and THEN rebuild TimelineData from it (or ensure assembleTimelineData sees the final config). Post-hoc mutation of an already-assembled TimelineData leaves stableSignature stale. The cleanest approach: materializeData returns a config, apply override to config, then pass to buildDataFromCurrentRegistry.\n\n3. **T10 (clip lifecycle)** is second highest risk. The plan says \"post-commit reconcile\" but that creates double history. Instead: make reconciliation part of materializeData itself. When it rebuilds rows, check if any pinned group clipIds reference clips no longer in the new rows. Clean them in the same data pass, before commitData. Zero extra undo entries.\n\n4. **T12 (grouped drag)** has THREE code paths to handle: (a) same-track multi-drag via type:'rows' \u2014 add pinnedShotGroupsOverride with updated trackId, (b) new-track multi-drag via buildConfigFromDragResult + type:'config' \u2014 inject pinnedShotGroups into the resolved config, (c) single-clip moveClipToRow in useTimelineTrackManagement \u2014 needs similar treatment. Read all three paths before coding.\n\n5. **T14 (shot drop)** \u2014 the existing handleAssetDrop is imperative and commits per asset. You MUST extract clip-building logic into a pure function or build clips inline. Do NOT call handleAssetDrop in a loop \u2014 that violates the single-applyEdit requirement.\n\n6. **T13 (shot drag type) has no dependencies** and can start in parallel with Phase 1.\n\n7. **T15 (auto-sync)** needs debouncing. Realtime shot image events can fire rapidly. Consider a 300ms debounce or batching within a single requestAnimationFrame.\n\n8. **Plan has duplicate steps**: Steps 13-14 are TODO placeholders that duplicate Steps 21-24. This finalize maps both sets to the concrete T13/T14/T15 tasks. Ignore the TODO versions.\n\n9. **Test strategy**: Don't create new test files except within existing test files.
